offering_description.value: Black Hills Corporation supplies natural gas and electricity to households, businesses and public agencies. It operates gas distribution and electric transmission and distribution networks, generates and purchases power, and mines coal in Wyoming for power generation.

primary_services.value: natural gas distribution and transportation; electricity distribution and transmission

customer_segment.value: B2C: Households buying natural gas or electricity; B2B: Commercial and industrial utility customers, wholesale power buyers and power plant operators; B2G: Local governments and public facilities buying utility service, including municipal street lighting

end_markets.value: residential energy; commercial buildings; industrial facilities; public infrastructure; electric utilities

revenue_model.value: product sales: Metered natural gas and electricity under utility tariffs, wholesale electricity and coal for power generation; transaction or usage fees: Gas transportation and electric transmission charges
revenue_model.category: product sales; transaction or usage fees

value_chain_position.value: asset operator: Operates gas pipelines, power plants and electric networks to serve utility customers and wholesale buyers; distributor: Delivers purchased gas and generated or purchased electricity to homes, businesses and public facilities; raw materials: Mines Wyoming coal for affiliated and neighboring power plants

geography_served.value: US regional: Arkansas, Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska, South Dakota and Wyoming

specialization.value: related lines: Natural gas utilities, electric utilities, power generation and coal mining that supports generation

distribution_channels.value: direct sales: Utility accounts served through company-operated gas and electric networks, plus direct wholesale supply arrangements

regulatory_exposure.value: high: State utility commissions regulate retail rates and service, and FERC oversees interstate electric transmission and wholesale power sales.

notes: This profile covers Black Hills on a standalone basis because the status of its announced NorthWestern Energy merger is uncertain.
